title: Search economy benchmark: agentic search vs code graph tools (graphify, codebase memory mcp) token cost
summary: Benchmark under bench/search-economy/ comparing context assembly arms on identical code navigation queries over the zonoid repo, scored by context tokens emitted plus recall and precision against ground truth relevant symbols (tokens per correct symbol). Arms span a substrate spectrum: naive (grep plus read, the baseline every tool benchmarks against), subconscious agentic search (vector RAG over the KB task graph, needs a repo source onboard first), codebase-memory-mcp (DeusData, hybrid AST knowledge graph plus local nomic-embed-code vector search, a single static binary with ZERO runtime deps that RUNS NOW on Windows via cli mode: codebase-memory-mcp cli index_repository / search_graph / trace_path / query_graph / get_code_snippet / search_code, JSON in JSON out), and graphify (pure AST graph, non vector, Python). Phase 1 retrieval first runs NOW in Node for naive, subconscious, and codebase-memory-mcp; graphify is deferred (needs Python). Phase 2 end to end on Terminal-Bench via a custom AbstractInstalledAgent adapter per arm (resolved rate plus total tokens from jobs trajectories) is scaffolded, run deferred (needs uv plus Docker). Key asymmetry the design controls for: subconscious indexes the KB task graph while codebase-memory-mcp and graphify index source code structure, so the fair unit is the SAME code nav query solved by different mechanisms, reported as a capability matrix not a single winner. Token claims to re measure on our own corpus and naive baseline: codebase-memory-mcp 99.2 percent reduction (3.4k vs 412k tokens, 5 structural queries vs grep); graphify 71x (1.7k vs 123k). Note name ambiguity: codebase memory mcp here means DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp; similarly named alternatives are kapillamba4/code-memory (Python uvx), tokensave, codegraph-mcp (Rust).
